children: Consumer sentiment for September was revised to

from the initial print of 47.8, declining from 51.7 in August, according to the University of Michigan Survey of Consumers on Friday. The current reading touched its lowest point in four months and has dropped 15% from January 2026.
Current economic conditions stayed at 50.9 vs. the initial print and slipped from 51.9 in August.
Consumer expectations were revised higher to 46.3 from the initial print of 45.8 but still represented a decline from 51.5 in the prior month.

"Views of current and year-ahead expected personal finances both weakened about 10% this month, with concerns over high prices continuing to climb," said Survey of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu. "Buying conditions for durables improved a bit, in part due to a perception that completing such purchases now would help consumers avoid higher prices in the future."

The outlook for businesses soured further in August. "The short-run outlook for business conditions plunged amid renewed worries that elevated fuel prices and re-escalating trade disputes could pass through to the economy as a whole," Hsu noted.
One-year inflation expectations of 4.6% were unrevised from the initial print. That compares with +4.0% in August.
Five-year implied inflation is still seen at +3.4% vs. +3.3% in the previous month.

title: Consumer sentiment September reading revised slightly higher but still falls from August
